newsitem.title: USA: Calif. senator introduces tobacco liability measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. senator introduces tobacco liability measure.

text.p: A California state senator on Wednesday introduced legislation to eliminate the special immunity from product liability lawsuits enjoyed by tobacco products in the state.

"This present exemption is an egregious example of special-interest legislation and is unjustified," said Sen. Quentin Kopp, a San Francisco independent. "The citizens of California should not have the right to recover for injury or death caused by tobacco products abrogated or impeded."
The exemption was part of 1987 legislation intended to forestall the number of product liability lawsuits by granting immunity to the manufacturers of certain products, Kopp said.
In addition to tobacco, other consumer products, including sugar, castor oil, alcohol and butter, were included in the immunity legislation, Kopp said.
Kopp said his proposed legislation, supported by the California Medical Association and other groups, only aims to eliminate the liability protection for tobacco products.

Attempting to recoup the cost of treating patients afflicted with smoking-related illnesses, a number of local governments in California, including the city and county of San Francisco, filed suit earlier this year against major tobacco companies.
A number of states also have filed suits against tobacco companies seeking to recover the health care costs of smokers.
